# pbs_network_interface (Resource)

Manages a network interface of a Proxmox Backup Server node in `/etc/network/interfaces`: a Linux bridge, a bond or a VLAN interface, which the resource creates, or a physical interface (`eth`), which it takes over.

!> **A wrong network setting cuts the node off, from Terraform and from you.** Changing the address, gateway, ports or MTU of the interface the provider reaches PBS through — or of one it runs on — can leave the node unreachable once the change is applied, and PBS keeps no copy of the previous configuration and does not roll back. Have the node's console at hand before changing interfaces it is reached through, and read the guide _Managing the network of a PBS node_.

**Changes are pending until applied.** PBS writes every change to `/etc/network/interfaces.new`, and none takes effect until the network is reloaded — with `pbs_network_apply`, or Apply Configuration in the web interface — or, from PBS 4.0.8, the node boots. The resource describes that file, pending changes included: while changes are pending, PBS reports the pending configuration, not the one the node runs.

**Creating needs root@pam.** PBS refuses to create an interface for every user but `root@pam` — an API token, even root@pam's, and any other user get `permission check failed`, whatever their ACL — so a configuration that creates — or replaces — bridges, bonds or VLAN interfaces needs the provider to sign in with `username = "root@pam"` and its `password`, and the plan fails otherwise. That is impossible when root@pam has two-factor authentication, which the provider cannot complete: create the interface on the node then — in the web interface, or with `proxmox-backup-manager network create` — and import it. Changing, deleting and reading existing interfaces, and taking over a physical one, need `Sys.Modify on /system/network/interfaces/<name>` and `Sys.Audit on /system/network/interfaces/<name>`, which an API token may have.

**A physical interface cannot be created or removed.** Creating the resource takes it over: it sets what the configuration sets, autostart included, which defaults to `true`, and removes the comments and MTU the configuration leaves out, with a warning in the plan. The plan refuses a takeover that would remove addresses or gateways, unless the configuration sets `method` (or `method6`) explicitly: import the interface instead, and write its settings into the configuration. Destroying the resource resets the interface to what PBS lists for a NIC the file does not configure: method `manual`, no addresses, comments or MTU, no autostart — PBS 4.1.7 and later keep an IPv6 method `dhcp` or `auto`. To stop managing an interface and leave it as it is — the one the node is reached through above all —, remove it from the state instead (a `removed` block with `destroy = false`, or `terraform state rm`). Lines of a stanza PBS does not interpret, such as `post-up` commands or `bridge-stp off`, are kept through every change; `options` and `options6` show them.

**Changes to several interfaces** are written one at a time, ports and slaves before the bridges and bonds that use them, and PBS checks the whole pending configuration at every write. So some changes take two applies, as the guide describes: removing a bond together with the bridge port it is, moving a NIC from a bridge into a new bond, raising the MTU of a bridge and its ports. Keep the network apply out of the first one, so that the node never runs the state in between.

**IPv4 DHCP.** PBS's API keeps only `static` and `manual` for IPv4: it turns any other IPv4 method, such as `dhcp`, into `manual` whenever it changes an interface. So a change of a bridge, bond or VLAN interface whose configuration sets `method = "dhcp"` replaces it — deletes it from the pending configuration and creates it anew, which needs root@pam and drops its `options` —, and the plan refuses to change an interface that has an IPv4 method other than `static` and `manual` when the configuration leaves `method` out, as it does to keep DHCP on a physical interface.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Creating interfaces needs root@pam, signed in with a password: PBS refuses
# to create one for anyone else, API tokens included. A root@pam with
# two-factor authentication cannot sign in through the provider: create the
# interfaces on the node then, and import them.
provider "pbs" {
  endpoint = "https://pbs.example.com:8007"
  username = "root@pam"
  password = var.pbs_root_password
}

# The node's two NICs, bonded with LACP, carry a VLAN-aware bridge for the
# backup network and, on VLAN 20 of that bridge, a storage network. The
# node is reached through another interface, which this leaves alone.
resource "pbs_network_interface" "bond0" {
  name                  = "bond0"
  type                  = "bond"
  slaves                = ["eno1", "eno2"]
  bond_mode             = "802.3ad"
  bond_xmit_hash_policy = "layer3+4"
  mtu                   = 9000
  comments              = "LACP to the core switches"
}

resource "pbs_network_interface" "vmbr1" {
  name              = "vmbr1"
  type              = "bridge"
  bridge_ports      = [pbs_network_interface.bond0.name]
  bridge_vlan_aware = true
  cidr              = "198.51.100.10/24"
  cidr6             = "2001:db8:100::10/64"
  mtu               = 9000
  comments          = "Backup network"
}

resource "pbs_network_interface" "storage" {
  name = "${pbs_network_interface.vmbr1.name}.20"
  type = "vlan"
  cidr = "203.0.113.10/24"
}

# A physical interface is taken over, not created: here a spare NIC gets a
# comment and stays down.
resource "pbs_network_interface" "eno3" {
  name      = "eno3"
  type      = "eth"
  autostart = false
  comments  = "Spare, not cabled"
}

# Nothing above takes effect until the pending changes are applied, after
# every interface is written.
resource "pbs_network_apply" "this" {
  triggers = {
    bond0   = jsonencode(pbs_network_interface.bond0)
    vmbr1   = jsonencode(pbs_network_interface.vmbr1)
    storage = jsonencode(pbs_network_interface.storage)
    eno3    = jsonencode(pbs_network_interface.eno3)
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the interface, up to 15 characters: an existing NIC's, such as `eno1`, for `eth`, or a new one, such as `vmbr1` or `bond0`. A VLAN interface named `<device>.<tag>`, such as `bond0.20`, or `vlan<tag>`, such as `vlan20`, takes its tag (and device) from the name, as PBS and ifupdown2 do; bridges and bonds must not have such names. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `type` (String) Type of the interface: `bridge`, `bond` or `vlan`, which the resource creates, or `eth`, a physical interface the node has, which it takes over. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `autostart` (Boolean) Whether the node brings the interface up at boot and when the network is reloaded (an `auto` line). Defaults to `true`: `ifreload -a`, which applies the changes, configures only such interfaces — and brings each of them in line with the file, removing addresses the file does not list, such as ones added by hand.
- `bond_mode` (String) Mode of a bond: `balance-rr`, `active-backup`, `balance-xor`, `broadcast`, `802.3ad` (LACP), `balance-tlb` or `balance-alb`. Defaults to `balance-rr`, as PBS does. Only for `bond`.
- `bond_primary` (String) Slave an `active-backup` bond prefers, one of `slaves`. Only with `bond_mode = "active-backup"`.
- `bond_xmit_hash_policy` (String) Transmit hash policy of an `802.3ad` or `balance-xor` bond: `layer2`, `layer2+3` or `layer3+4`. Left out, the kernel's default (`layer2`) applies.
- `bridge_ports` (Set of String) Ports of a bridge, such as `["eno1"]` or a bond; left out, the bridge has none (`bridge-ports none`). PBS refuses ports that do not exist and ports another bridge or bond uses. Only for `bridge`.
- `bridge_vlan_aware` (Boolean) Whether a bridge is VLAN-aware. Defaults to `false`. Only for `bridge`.
- `cidr` (String) IPv4 address with its prefix length, such as `192.0.2.10/24`.
- `cidr6` (String) IPv6 address with its prefix length, such as `2001:db8::10/64`.
- `comments` (String) Comment of the interface, shown in the web interface; several lines are fine. PBS writes each as a `#` line of the IPv4 stanza and reads it back trimmed, so no line may begin or end with white space.
- `comments6` (String) Comment of the IPv6 stanza, which PBS keeps apart; it makes PBS write an `inet6` stanza even when `method6` is `manual`.
- `gateway` (String) IPv4 default gateway, such as `192.0.2.1`. PBS allows one IPv4 gateway in the whole configuration and refuses a second.
- `gateway6` (String) IPv6 default gateway, such as `2001:db8::1` or `fe80::1`. PBS allows one IPv6 gateway in the whole configuration.
- `method` (String) IPv4 method: `static` with an address or gateway, `manual` without, or `dhcp`, for a bridge, bond or VLAN interface only, which then has to be replaced to change (see above). Left out, it follows from `cidr` and `gateway`; an existing interface keeps another method it has, such as `dhcp`, which the plan then refuses to change, and a new one gets `manual`.
- `method6` (String) IPv6 method: `static` with an address or gateway, `manual` without, `dhcp` (PBS 4.1.7 and later) or `auto` — SLAAC, from router advertisements (PBS 4.2.7 and later). Left out, it follows from `cidr6` and `gateway6`, and keeps `dhcp` or `auto` for an interface that has it. Older PBS releases turn `dhcp` and `auto` into `manual` on any change of an interface, and those before 4.2.7 cannot read a configuration with `auto` at all.
- `mtu` (Number) MTU in bytes, 68 to 65535. Left out, the file sets none and the kernel's default applies — 1500 for Ethernet. PBS refuses a port or slave whose MTU is larger than its bridge's or bond's, counting a bridge without an MTU as 1500; a bond without one takes any. To raise the MTU of a bridge and its ports, raise the bridge's in one apply and the ports' in the next.
- `node` (String) Node whose interface to manage: `localhost`, which every PBS answers to, or the node's host name. Defaults to the provider's `node`. Both name the same node: manage each interface with one resource only. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `slaves` (List of String) Physical interfaces of a bond, in order; left out, the bond has none (`bond-slaves none`). PBS refuses slaves that are not physical (`eth`) interfaces of the node and slaves another bridge or bond uses. Only for `bond`.
- `vlan_id` (Number) Tag of a VLAN interface, 1 to 4094. Required unless the name gives it (`<device>.<tag>` or `vlan<tag>`), and then, if set, the same. PBS cannot remove it, so removing it replaces the resource. Only for `vlan`.
- `vlan_raw_device` (String) Interface a VLAN interface runs on, such as `bond0`, which must exist. Required unless the name gives it (`<device>.<tag>`), and then, if set, the same. PBS cannot remove it, so removing it replaces the resource. Only for `vlan`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<node>/<name>`, such as `localhost/vmbr1`.
- `options` (List of String) Lines of the IPv4 stanza PBS does not interpret, such as `bridge-stp off` or `post-up` commands, verbatim. The resource neither sets nor removes them, and PBS keeps them through every change, but a replacement creates the interface without them.
- `options6` (List of String) Lines of the IPv6 stanza PBS does not interpret, verbatim.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_network_interface.vmbr0
  identity = {
    node = "localhost"
    name = "vmbr0"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `name` (String) Interface name, such as `vmbr1`.
- `node` (String) Node name, such as `localhost`.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_network_interface.vmbr0
  id = "localhost/vmbr0"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# An interface is imported by <node>/<name>: the node is localhost or the
# node's host name.
terraform import pbs_network_interface.vmbr0 localhost/vmbr0
```
